projects.title: Wireless Battery Management System
projects.summary: A wireless BMS PCB that monitors a 14-series lithium-ion pack using a TI BQ79616-Q1. Each node is paired with a CC2652R7 radio that sends readings over a custom 2.4 GHz link, as opposed to the usual isolated daisy-chain wiring.

gallery.caption: PCB bring-up: 58 V stack supply, LaunchPad receiver, live packet stream
Two PCBs connected at different supply voltages
Both resistor-divider segments receiving cell voltages and NTC temperature readings on one channel

highlights: Utilized an embedded 2.4 GHz PCB antenna with an 0201-component impedance-matching network.
Transmitted from two PCBs at the same time on one channel, each identified by its factory MAC address.
Implemented a buck converter and LDO combination that converted the stack voltage to 5 V and 3.3 V supply rails.

projects.title: Wireless Songbird PIR Sensor
projects.summary: A wireless PCB that tracks songbird activity for Columbia labs, using a PIR motion sensor, Li-Po battery circuitry, and a TI CC1310 Sub-GHz radio module. Each node sends motion detection counts, live battery data, and its cage ID over a 433 MHz link.

gallery.caption: Power profile: 337 µA average with 20 mA current spikes during each packet transmission, sent every 3 minutes
PCBA and 820 mAh Li-Po inside a 3D-printed enclosure
Sensor node mounted on a songbird cage

highlights: Measured a 337 µA average current draw with a power analyzer, then sized the Li-Po down to 820 mAh to cut BOM cost while still achieving a 100-day battery life.
Utilized accelerometer data to switch between monitoring and a low-power ready-to-charge state, depending on the sensor node's current position.
Designed a second EEPROM PCB that remains on each cage and plugs into the sensor's USB-C charging port, allowing the sensor to tag every packet with the cage's hardcoded ID.
Managed production of 100 PCBAs through JLCPCB, coordinating part selection and Li-Po battery orders.

projects.title: 12 GHz Low-Noise Amplifier
projects.summary: A two-stage GaAs low-noise amplifier for the 11.4–12.7 GHz Ku-band Starlink downlink, designed and simulated in Keysight ADS on Rogers RT/duroid 5880.

specs.caption: Simulated in Keysight ADS
specs.note: Small-signal results use the transistor's S-parameter data. The nonlinear model was used for compression, IP3, and DC power.

gallery.caption: Stabilizing the transistor: a 450 Ω gate shunt resistor keeps the stability factor above 1 from 0.1 to 20 GHz
Stage 1 matched for minimum noise: 0.685 dB noise figure at 12 GHz
Final two-stage schematic with radial-stub bias feeds and a coupled-line interstage DC block
Simulated gain, noise figure, input and output match, and stability from 0.1 to 20 GHz

highlights: Selected the NE3210S01 from four candidate GaAs transistors for its low 0.34 dB NFmin and high 13.5 dB associated gain at the target 12 GHz.
Stabilized each stage with a 450 Ω gate shunt resistor by identifying the largest value that kept μ above 1 from 0.1 to 20 GHz while minimizing the amount of added noise.
Noise-matched the first stage to Γopt to minimize the cascaded noise figure and gain-matched the second stage with noise/gain circles to achieve the required gain.
